1.explanation: This script demonstrates how the report-renderer checks for a non-empty “runtimeWarnings” array in the Lighthouse JSON and, if present, emits the warning banner at the top of the report body. By loading a known sample result, manually populating `sampleResults.runtimeWarnings` with the headless-Chrome warning text, and then calling `ReportGeneratorV2.generateReportHtml()`, you will get an HTML file that reproduces exactly the bug scenario shown in your screenshot.
1.bug_scenario:
When Lighthouse generates a report from results that include an entry in the “runtimeWarnings” array (for example, when running under headless Chrome, which cannot apply mobile network throttling), the report-renderer inserts a prominent warning banner directly under the category gauges in the report header. The banner reads something like:

  “⚠️ Note: Your site’s mobile performance may be worse than the numbers presented in this report. Lighthouse could not test on a mobile connection because Headless Chrome does not support network throttling. See crbug.com/728451.”

In the screenshot you provided, you can see the 36/98/97/77 gauge row followed immediately by that red warning note across the full report width.
